newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close up in near-record volume.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close up in near-record volume.

text.p: French stocks ended an extremely active session higher on Tuesday, bolstered by a turnaround on Wall Street and firmer European bond prices.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 22.56 points, or 0.82 percent, at 2,784.76, while the CAC-40 June futures contract rose 11 points to 2,770.
Volume totalled 17.56 billion francs, the second-highest daily level after the record 17.97 billion franc volume set on May 30 of this year.
Turnover was swelled by several huge block trades in blue chip stocks including Total, Elf Aquitaine, Rhone Poulenc, and Alcatel Alsthom at the start of the new monthly account.

The bourse closed off its highs, reached after European Monetary Affairs Commission Yves-Thibault de Silguy said the Maastricht criterion for monetary union of 3.0 percent of gross domestic product would not be brutally applied.
Prices slipped back after Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said the audit of public finances would probably reveal a greater than expected public deficit, brokers said.
Shares in Moulinex surged 6.33 percent to 159.50 francs after brokerage Cholet Dupont raised its earnings estimates for the appliance maker and its stock rating to buy from hold.

Luxury goods group LVMH's stock slipped 1.33 percent to 1,483 francs after nudging up its stake in Grand Metropolitan Plc to 6.3 percent as part of an effort to block a planned merger between Grand Met and Guinness.
